metadata.headline: Where an Artist Draws a Crowd, and the Crowd Draws the Artist
metadata.speaker: am

sentences.sentence: The violinist Jennifer Koh stood at the center of an illustrator’s studio in Brooklyn on a recent evening and dug into the opening chords of Bach’s Chaconne.
I was too busy trying to capture the tilt of her pink-coiffed head on the chin rest and the curve of her shoulder, which flexed and dipped with each stroke of her bow.
Occasionally, I stole glances at the more confident sketches materializing on desks around me.
As I worked tentative lines onto the page, my eyes darting between my drawing and the ever-changing shape of my subject, I felt confronted with the limits of my attention.

I had joined Seen Here, a monthly series organized by the illustrator Julia Rothman and the journalist Joshua David Stein, in which performers — flamenco dancers, a balloon sculptor and now a violinist — are invited to demonstrate and talk about their work while a roomful of professional and amateur artists tries to render them in the medium of their choice.
For most, it is figure drawing with a twist.
For me, it was a chance to set aside my usual music critic’s tool kit — ears, words, judgment — to experience a performance with my eyes.
